differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Laryngoscopy shows paradoxical vocal cord adduction during inspiration; asthma has reversible airflow obstruction on spirometry.

differential_diagnoses.name: Heart failure
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Elevated BNP and echocardiographic evidence of left ventricular dysfunction; asthma has normal BNP and reversible airflow obstruction.

differential_diagnoses.name: Foreign body aspiration
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Unilateral wheeze and hyperinflation on chest X-ray; asthma typically has bilateral wheezing and reversible obstruction.

key_features: Episodic wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and cough, often triggered by allergens, exercise, cold air, or infections.
Reversible airflow obstruction on spirometry: FEV1 increases ≥12% and ≥200 mL after bronchodilator.
Evidence of airway hyperresponsiveness on methacholine challenge or peak flow variability.
Elevated fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) or sputum eosinophilia in allergic asthma.
Symptoms often worse at night or early morning.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for COPD because both cause wheezing and airflow obstruction; asthma is differentiated by significant reversibility with bronchodilators and often a history of atopy.
The diagnosis is missed when cough-variant asthma is attributed to postnasal drip or GERD without spirometry or bronchodilator response testing.

differential_diagnoses.name: Measles
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Koplik spots on buccal mucosa and rash that starts on face and spreads downward, with high fever persisting during rash.

differential_diagnoses.name: Rubella
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Posterior auricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy, rash spreads from face to trunk, and fever is low-grade.

differential_diagnoses.name: Scarlet fever
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Sandpaper-like rash with circumoral pallor, strawberry tongue, and positive throat culture for group A Streptococcus.

differential_diagnoses.name: Drug eruption
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: History of new medication exposure and rash often polymorphous, without the characteristic defervescence followed by rash.

differential_diagnoses.name: Fifth disease (erythema infectiosum)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Slapped-cheek facial rash and reticular rash on extremities, with no high fever.

key_features: High fever (often >39.5°C) for 3-5 days in a child aged 6-24 months.
Defervescence followed by appearance of a rose-pink maculopapular rash on trunk and neck.
Rash is non-pruritic and fades within 1-2 days.
Mild pharyngitis and lymphadenopathy may be present.
Caused by human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) or HHV-7.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for measles or rubella because of fever and rash, but rash appears after fever subsides rather than during fever.
The febrile phase without rash is often misdiagnosed as a viral upper respiratory infection or urinary tract infection.

differential_diagnoses.name: Psoriasis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Well-demarcated plaques with silvery scale, often on extensor surfaces, and positive Auspitz sign (pinpoint bleeding on scale removal).

differential_diagnoses.name: Tinea corporis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Annular lesion with central clearing and active scaly border; KOH preparation shows fungal hyphae.

differential_diagnoses.name: Contact dermatitis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Sharp demarcation corresponding to area of contact with allergen/irritant; patch testing can identify cause.

differential_diagnoses.name: Seborrheic dermatitis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Greasy yellowish scales on scalp, eyebrows, and nasolabial folds; responds to antifungal shampoo.

differential_diagnoses.name: Scabies
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Intense pruritus worse at night, burrows in web spaces, and mites/eggs on skin scraping.

key_features: Pruritic, erythematous, scaly, and often vesicular lesions.
Lichenification in chronic cases due to scratching.
Distribution varies by type: flexural in atopic dermatitis, extensor in nummular, etc.
Personal or family history of atopy (asthma, allergic rhinitis) in atopic dermatitis.
Elevated serum IgE and eosinophilia may be present in atopic dermatitis.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for psoriasis or tinea because of scaling and erythema, but lack of silvery scale and negative KOH help differentiate.
Secondary bacterial infection (impetiginization) can be missed when crusting and oozing are attributed solely to eczema.

differential_diagnoses.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Symmetrical small joint involvement (MCP, PIP), prolonged morning stiffness >1 hour, and positive rheumatoid factor/anti-CCP antibodies.

differential_diagnoses.name: Gout
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Acute monoarthritis with severe pain, erythema, and negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals in synovial fluid.

differential_diagnoses.name: Pseudogout (CPPD)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Positively birefringent rhomboid crystals in synovial fluid and chondrocalcinosis on X-ray.

differential_diagnoses.name: Psoriatic arthritis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Dactylitis, nail pitting, and skin psoriasis; asymmetric involvement and negative rheumatoid factor.

differential_diagnoses.name: Septic arthritis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Fever, marked joint erythema and warmth, and synovial fluid with >50,000 WBCs/mm3 and positive Gram stain/culture.

key_features: Joint pain worsened with activity and relieved by rest.
Brief morning stiffness (<30 minutes).
Bony enlargement (Heberden's and Bouchard's nodes) and crepitus on movement.
Asymmetric involvement of weight-bearing joints (knees, hips) and first carpometacarpal joint.
Radiographs show joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and cysts.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for rheumatoid arthritis because of joint pain and stiffness, but OA lacks systemic inflammation and has negative autoantibodies.
Septic arthritis can be missed in patients with pre-existing OA who present with acute worsening of joint pain.

differential_diagnoses.name: Von Willebrand disease
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Prolonged bleeding time and low von Willebrand factor antigen/activity; normal factor VIII level (unless type 2N).

differential_diagnoses.name: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Isolated thrombocytopenia with normal PT/PTT and increased bleeding with petechiae, not hemarthroses.

differential_diagnoses.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Prolonged PT and PTT, low platelets, elevated D-dimer, and schistocytes on smear.

differential_diagnoses.name: Factor XI deficiency
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Prolonged PTT with normal PT and bleeding after surgery/trauma, but factor XI assay is low.

differential_diagnoses.name: Liver disease
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Prolonged PT and PTT that correct with vitamin K or fresh frozen plasma, with elevated liver enzymes.

key_features: Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) with normal prothrombin time (PT) and platelet count.
Spontaneous hemarthroses (especially knees, elbows, ankles) and deep muscle bleeds.
Prolonged bleeding after trauma or surgery.
X-linked recessive inheritance; mostly males affected.
Low factor VIII (hemophilia A) or factor IX (hemophilia B) activity.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for von Willebrand disease because both cause mucosal bleeding, but hemophilia typically presents with hemarthroses and normal bleeding time.
Mild hemophilia may be missed until provoked bleeding occurs, as aPTT can be only mildly prolonged.

differential_diagnoses.name: Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: More extensive epidermal detachment (>30% body surface area) and higher mortality; SJS has <10% detachment.

differential_diagnoses.name: Erythema multiforme major
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Target lesions predominantly on extremities, often triggered by infections (e.g., HSV), with less mucosal involvement and no widespread epidermal necrosis.

differential_diagnoses.name: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Superficial epidermal peeling (Nikolsky sign positive) without mucosal involvement, caused by staphylococcal toxin, and intraepidermal cleavage on biopsy.

differential_diagnoses.name: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Prominent eosinophilia, systemic organ involvement (liver, kidney), and later onset (2-8 weeks) without significant epidermal detachment.

differential_diagnoses.name: Pemphigus vulgaris
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Flaccid bullae and mucosal erosions, with intraepidermal acantholysis and positive anti-desmoglein antibodies.

key_features: Prodrome of fever and malaise followed by painful erythematous macules that coalesce and develop bullae.
Mucosal involvement (oral, ocular, genital) in >90% of cases.
Positive Nikolsky sign (epidermal detachment with lateral pressure).
Epidermal detachment <10% body surface area (SJS) or 10-30% (SJS/TEN overlap).
Often triggered by medications (e.g., sulfonamides, anticonvulsants, allopurinol) within 1-3 weeks.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for erythema multiforme because of target-like lesions, but SJS has widespread mucosal involvement and epidermal necrosis.
Early stage can be misdiagnosed as a viral exanthem or drug rash when mucosal signs are subtle.

differential_diagnoses.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone and androstenedione, with virilization in females and salt-wasting in severe forms; cortisol is low.

differential_diagnoses.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Elevated LH/FSH ratio, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, and insulin resistance; estrogen levels are normal or elevated, not low.

differential_diagnoses.name: Androgen-secreting ovarian tumor
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Rapid virilization, markedly elevated testosterone or DHEAS, and pelvic mass on imaging.

differential_diagnoses.name: Turner syndrome
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Short stature, webbed neck, and karyotype 45,X; estrogen deficiency with elevated FSH/LH but no virilization.

differential_diagnoses.name: Idiopathic hirsutism
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Hirsutism with normal androgen levels and regular ovulation; no virilization or estrogen deficiency.

key_features: Virilization in females (hirsutism, clitoromegaly, deepening voice) due to elevated androgens.
Low serum estradiol with elevated FSH and LH.
Elevated testosterone and androstenedione.
In males, tall stature, delayed bone age, and osteoporosis due to estrogen deficiency.
Caused by mutations in the CYP19A1 gene.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for PCOS because of hirsutism and menstrual irregularities, but estrogen levels are low and virilization is progressive.
In males, the diagnosis is often missed because estrogen deficiency presents subtly with tall stature and bone pain.

differential_diagnoses.name: Ventricular septal defect (VSD)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Harsh holosystolic murmur at left lower sternal border; echocardiogram shows defect in ventricular septum.

differential_diagnoses.name: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Continuous machinery murmur at left infraclavicular area; echocardiogram shows ductal flow.

differential_diagnoses.name: Mitral stenosis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Diastolic rumbling murmur at apex with opening snap; echocardiogram shows restricted mitral valve opening.

differential_diagnoses.name: Pulmonary stenosis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Ejection systolic murmur at left upper sternal border with systolic click; echocardiogram shows increased pulmonary valve gradient.

differential_diagnoses.name: Physiologic murmur
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Soft systolic murmur, normal split S2, and no echocardiographic defect.

key_features: Fixed split S2 on auscultation.
Systolic ejection murmur at left upper sternal border due to increased pulmonary flow.
Right ventricular heave and signs of right heart failure in advanced cases.
Echocardiogram shows defect in atrial septum with left-to-right shunt.
ECG may show right axis deviation and incomplete right bundle branch block.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for a physiologic murmur or VSD because of the systolic murmur, but fixed split S2 is characteristic.
In adults, ASD may be misdiagnosed as pulmonary hypertension or coronary disease when presenting with dyspnea and right heart failure.

differential_diagnoses.name: Vestibular neuritis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Acute prolonged vertigo with nausea and horizontal nystagmus, without positional triggering; positive head impulse test.

differential_diagnoses.name: Meniere's disease
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Episodic vertigo lasting hours with fluctuating hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness.

differential_diagnoses.name: Orthostatic hypotension
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Dizziness on standing with a drop in blood pressure, not triggered by head rotation.

differential_diagnoses.name: Central positional vertigo
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Nystagmus that is vertical or direction-changing, without latency or fatigability; often with neurological signs.

differential_diagnoses.name: Acoustic neuroma
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Unilateral hearing loss and tinnitus; MRI shows cerebellopontine angle mass.

key_features: Brief episodes of rotational vertigo triggered by changes in head position (e.g., rolling over in bed).
Positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver eliciting vertigo and torsional nystagmus with latency and fatigability.
No hearing loss or neurological symptoms.
Canalith repositioning maneuvers (e.g., Epley) are effective.
Often self-limited, resolving within weeks.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for vestibular neuritis or Meniere's disease because of recurrent vertigo, but BPPV is strictly positional and short-lived.
Central causes of positional vertigo (e.g., brainstem lesion) can be missed if nystagmus characteristics are not carefully assessed.

differential_diagnoses.name: Schizophrenia
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Presence of frank psychotic symptoms (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech) for ≥6 months with functional decline.

differential_diagnoses.name: Autism spectrum disorder
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Early childhood onset of social communication deficits and restricted interests, without the magical thinking and perceptual distortions typical of schizotypal disorder.

differential_diagnoses.name: Social anxiety disorder
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Fear of negative evaluation in social situations, but no magical thinking, odd beliefs, or perceptual distortions.

differential_diagnoses.name: Schizoid personality disorder
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Social isolation and restricted affect without the cognitive-perceptual distortions (e.g., magical thinking, ideas of reference) seen in schizotypal.

differential_diagnoses.name: Avoidant personality disorder
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Hypersensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social interaction due to fear of criticism, without odd beliefs or eccentric behavior.

key_features: Ideas of reference (excluding delusions of reference).
Odd beliefs or magical thinking (e.g., superstitions, belief in clairvoyance).
Unusual perceptual experiences (e.g., bodily illusions).
Odd thinking and speech (e.g., vague, metaphorical, overelaborate).
Suspiciousness or paranoid ideation, and inappropriate or constricted affect.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for schizophrenia because of odd beliefs and perceptual experiences, but schizotypal disorder lacks sustained psychotic symptoms.
May be misdiagnosed as social anxiety disorder when social withdrawal is prominent, missing the cognitive-perceptual features.

differential_diagnoses.name: Psoriasis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Well-demarcated plaques with silvery scale, often on extensor surfaces, and responds to topical corticosteroids; biopsy shows regular acanthosis without atypia.

differential_diagnoses.name: Nummular eczema
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Intensely pruritic coin-shaped lesions with oozing and crusting; biopsy shows spongiosis, not full-thickness atypia.

differential_diagnoses.name: Superficial basal cell carcinoma
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Pearly rolled border with telangiectasia; biopsy shows basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and clefting.

differential_diagnoses.name: Tinea corporis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Annular lesion with central clearing and active scaly border; KOH preparation positive for fungal hyphae.

differential_diagnoses.name: Actinic keratosis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Rough, scaly macule on sun-exposed skin; biopsy shows atypia confined to lower epidermis, not full thickness.

key_features: Slow-growing, well-demarcated, erythematous, scaly plaque, often on sun-exposed areas.
May be mistaken for eczema or psoriasis but does not respond to topical steroids.
Biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal atypia (squamous cell carcinoma in situ) with intact basement membrane.
Risk of progression to invasive squamous cell carcinoma (3-5%).
Associated with chronic sun exposure, arsenic, or HPV infection.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for eczema or psoriasis because of scaly erythematous plaques, leading to delayed biopsy and diagnosis.
May be misdiagnosed as actinic keratosis when atypia is not full-thickness on inadequate biopsy.

differential_diagnoses.name: Conduct disorder
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Presence of more severe antisocial behaviors (e.g., aggression, theft, destruction) violating rights of others, beyond defiance.

differential_diagnoses.name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Core symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, not primarily anger/defiance; often comorbid but distinct.

differential_diagnoses.name: Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD)
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Chronic severe irritability with frequent temper outbursts out of proportion to situation, with persistent negative mood between outbursts.

differential_diagnoses.name: Intermittent explosive disorder
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Recurrent impulsive aggressive outbursts without the persistent pattern of defiance and argumentativeness.

differential_diagnoses.name: Autism spectrum disorder
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Social communication deficits and restricted interests; defiance may occur but is not the primary feature.

key_features: Pattern of angry/irritable mood, argumentative/defiant behavior, or vindictiveness lasting ≥6 months.
Often argues with authority figures and actively defies or refuses to comply with requests.
Deliberately annoys others and blames others for mistakes.
Symptoms cause distress or impairment in social, academic, or occupational functioning.
Not better explained by another mental disorder (e.g., conduct disorder, ADHD).
pitfalls: Often mistaken for conduct disorder because of behavioral problems, but ODD lacks severe violations of others' rights.
May be misdiagnosed as ADHD when impulsivity and defiance co-occur, missing the primary mood and defiance pattern.

differential_diagnoses.name: Cocaine intoxication
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Short duration of action (minutes to hours), presence of cocaine metabolites on urine drug screen, and possible nasal septal damage.

differential_diagnoses.name: Methamphetamine intoxication
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Longer duration than cocaine, positive amphetamine screen, and often associated with skin picking and dental decay.

differential_diagnoses.name: Serotonin syndrome
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Clonus, hyperreflexia, and agitation after serotonergic drugs; not typically associated with amphetamine-positive urine.

differential_diagnoses.name: Thyrotoxicosis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Elevated free T4 and low TSH, with goiter and weight loss; no amphetamine on drug screen.

differential_diagnoses.name: Panic attack
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Sudden intense fear with palpitations and diaphoresis, but no hypertension or tachycardia beyond typical panic, and no amphetamine exposure.

key_features: Tachycardia, hypertension, and hyperthermia.
Agitation, tremor, and hyperreflexia.
Mydriasis and dry mucous membranes.
Insomnia and decreased appetite.
Positive amphetamine on urine drug screen (lisdexamfetamine is a prodrug of dextroamphetamine).
pitfalls: Often mistaken for cocaine or methamphetamine intoxication because of sympathomimetic symptoms, but lisdexamfetamine has a longer duration and is a prodrug.
Therapeutic use of lisdexamfetamine for ADHD may be overlooked, leading to misattribution of symptoms to illicit drugs.

differential_diagnoses.name: Ectopic pregnancy
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Positive pregnancy test and ultrasound showing extrauterine gestational sac; risk of rupture and hemoperitoneum.

differential_diagnoses.name: Appendicitis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Migratory right lower quadrant pain, positive McBurney point tenderness, and CT showing inflamed appendix.

differential_diagnoses.name: Ovarian torsion
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Sudden severe unilateral pelvic pain with nausea and vomiting; ultrasound shows enlarged ovary with decreased blood flow.

differential_diagnoses.name: Urinary tract infection
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Dysuria, frequency, and positive urine culture, without cervical motion tenderness.

differential_diagnoses.name: Endometriosis
differential_diagnoses.distinguishing_feature: Cyclic pelvic pain and dysmenorrhea, with endometrial glands/stroma on biopsy; no fever or purulent discharge.

key_features: Lower abdominal and pelvic pain.
Cervical motion tenderness, uterine tenderness, or adnexal tenderness on bimanual exam.
Abnormal vaginal or cervical discharge, often purulent.
Fever and elevated white blood cell count.
Positive nucleic acid amplification test for Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
pitfalls: Often mistaken for appendicitis or urinary tract infection because of abdominal pain, but cervical motion tenderness and discharge point to PID.
Subclinical PID may be missed when symptoms are mild, leading to long-term complications like infertility.
